quotes.text: Directly exposing SQL data to the cloud is corporate self-harm. Firewalls, network zones, and authentication boundaries exist precisely because someone once tried just opening a port and spent the next quarter explaining the breach.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why on-prem data must stay behind the firewall.

quotes.text: The gateway maintains sovereignty by initiating every conversation outward, picture it like an employee who only makes phone calls. They never accept incoming ones.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple analogy for the gateway's outbound-only security model.

quotes.text: No, the gateway does not upload your database. It doesn't clone, mirror, or replicate anything. All it does is execute queries on your behalf and return the results
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Answers the most common security objection to the gateway.

quotes.text: Many organizations sensibly divide knowledge and action credentials. Reading might use a service account with select rights only while writing requires an elevated connector approved by IT.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete separation-of-duties recommendation for AI write-backs.

quotes.text: Moving your crown jewel data to someone else's cloud isn't modernization. It's surrender. The goal is synchronization without exposure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's hybrid philosophy in three short sentences.

chapters.title: The data gateway as the spine of hybrid AI
Adding SQL as a knowledge source

takeaways: The on-premises data gateway lets Copilot Studio query and update on-prem SQL Server through outbound-only, encrypted connections without copying the database to the cloud.
Expose only well-named, read-optimized views as knowledge sources and clearly labeled parameters for SQL actions, so the agent queries precisely and asks for missing inputs.
Use gateway clusters for resilience, separate read and write credentials, and export Power Platform telemetry for auditing.
hook: Copilot Studio agents sound confident but cannot see the customer and order data that lives in on-prem SQL Server. This episode shows Power Platform makers and architects how to connect SQL through the on-premises data gateway as a knowledge source and with write-back actions, without opening the firewall or moving the data.
